thread:
Alex: Quick check — planning a small change to embeddings ingest behavior. Current truncation/shape questions: per-item truncation limit, how we treat non-string items, and whether we should surface a per-item 'truncated' flag. cc @Maya @Cheng

Maya: What exactly are we changing? I thought we already truncate per-item at 8192 chars and always return one vector per input.

Cheng: Current contract we implemented in runtime: items can be string or object (we stringify non-strings). If string >8192 bytes we truncate to 8192 before tokenization. We intended to add per-item metadata but didn't finalize the API field.

Lina: Where is that behavior documented? I can't find a clear mention in openapi or the public docs.

Alex: Not in public docs yet. Decision points: add an optional boolean 'truncated' per item + maybe 'original_length' int? Keep array length identical. Also ensure SDKs remain backwards compatible.

InfraBot: deploy-bot: dev/embeddings-api v1.12 deployed to staging at 1729087700 :rocket:

Maya: Additive fields are fine. We must avoid breaking older SDKs that do strict shape checks (mobile is suspicious). If fields are optional it should be safe.

Cheng: Proposal: response stays as array with same length. Each entry becomes {"vector": [...], "truncated": true?, "input_length": 1234?}. Both new keys optional.

Alex: Good. Can someone run a quick fuzz on mixed batches: ["", null, {obj}, very long string (>32k), emoji-heavy multibyte] — ensure coercion, truncation, and shape are stable. Also check that an empty string still returns a vector and that null becomes 'null' string consistently.

Lina: Will run staged tests. Need a curl example to reproduce locally?

Cheng: curl example:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"items":["", null, {"title":"hi"}, "LONG_STRING_HERE_WITH_EMOJI_𝌆𝌆"]}'

Maya: Also confirm batch limits: last I saw it's 1024 items or ~10MB payload. If we stringify objects they count toward payload size.

Alex: Right — we should call out payload sizing in the docs. Plan: Lina run tests and post results by EOD, Cheng open PR adding optional fields + docs, Maya run a quick client scan for brittle deserializers, I'll draft release notes and oncall handover. If no blockers, target shipping Thursday.

Lina: Quick results from staging: empty string -> vector OK; null coerced to "null" string -> vector OK; long string trimmed and vector produced; truncated items show "truncated": true when hitting 8192 bytes. Found one issue: objects with nested arrays where the serialized string exceeds 8192 were not being truncated correctly (server error path). Filed issue #3489 and attached failing payload.

Alex: Can you paste the failing payload snippet + short stack trace?

Lina: failing payload snippet:
{"items":[{"docs": ["very long... repeated" * 2000]}]}
stack snippet: `runtime: panic: index out of range at kvcache.go:412` — repro attached in issue.

Cheng: I'll take #3489. Likely an off-by-one in the serializer->trunc path when handling arrays. Will push a fix and redeploy to staging, update the PR.

Maya: FYI mobile SDK for iOS uses a strict Codable model that expects an object with only vector array. Adding fields is ok if we use ignoreUnknownKeys, but I'll ping mobile to confirm.

Alex: @oncall — please note potential transient errors during the next staging deploy.

InfraBot: oncall: @Sara assigned for next 24h

Sara: Oncall ack. I'll watch embed-api errors and paging metrics (5xx and latency).

Alex: Thanks everyone. Cheng — once fix lands and QA passes, ping me and I'll merge release notes and tag the PR.

Maya: Also can we add a small compatibility note in the SDKs changelog: "response may include optional per-item metadata (truncated, input_length) — SDKs should ignore unknown keys".

Cheng: Will include that.

Alex: Great — that's the plan. Lina please follow up with the issue link and test artifacts in the ticket.

Lina: Will do, posting artifacts now. :white_check_mark:
